_readme.what: Indian proper nouns and loanwords -> IPA, injected as <phoneme alphabet="ipa"> into the en-US story narration by tools/tts.py. Hindi/Punjabi clips do NOT use this file: those voices are already native.
_readme.goal: The narrator keeps her English (diaspora) accent; the Indian names are said the way an Indian family says them. Not Sanskrit-pedantic, not anglicised.
engine_limits: Google's en-US phoneme set is the American English one. Symbols outside it are not an error - the API silently drops the <phoneme> tag and reads the spelling instead. Every entry here was verified against the live API on a decoy spelling, which is the only test that can tell 'honoured' from 'thrown away'. Run tools/tts.py --check-lexicon to redo it.

ASPIRATION IS RENDERABLE, and an earlier pass was wrong to say it was not. That mistake is why every Indian name in the narration was anglicised: Bhima came out 'Beema', Bharata 'Burrutuh'. Probed and accepted: bʰ ɡʰ kʰ dʒʰ tʃʰ ʈʰ ɖʰ, and the DENTAL pair d̪ʰ t̪ʰ. Do not 'simplify' d̪ʰ to dʰ or t̪ʰ to tʰ: bare dʰ and tʰ are REJECTED, and the dental diacritic U+032A is what makes the API accept them. The aspiration mark itself must be U+02B0 ʰ; the breathy-voice sign U+02B1 ʱ is rejected.
Two aspirates still have no accepted form and are written plain, with a note on the entry saying so: pʰ (so phad is pəɖ) and ɽʰ (so the -garh of Chandigarh is ɡəɽ).

Aspiration is realised as ENGLISH allophonic aspiration, so it is suppressed after a sibilant exactly as in English 'star'. Yudhishthira and Vasishtha keep their ʈʰ - the tag is honoured, the puff simply does not survive the ʂ. Nothing to fix; do not remove the mark.

PRIMARY STRESS MAY NOT FALL ON ə - probed and confirmed, ˈə is rejected outright. This is the trap that produced the old file: rather than move the stress, it changed the vowel to ʌ, the 'cup' vowel, and that single substitution is most of what made the names sound English. The rule now is the other way round - short Indian 'a' is ALWAYS ə, and the stress mark goes. Indian languages do not carry an English-shaped accent on a short a anyway, so nothing is lost.
Retroflexes ʈ ɖ ɳ ɽ ʂ are accepted and kept where they change the word. ʋ is accepted and is used for both v and w, which are one sound in most of India.
Long vowels are written with ː. Indian monophthongs are written eː / oː rather than the American diphthongs eɪ / oʊ where the difference is audible.
_readme.format: "Term": { "ipa": "...", "note": "plain-English respelling, CAPS = the syllable leaned on", "unsure": true (only where the reading is genuinely in doubt) }. The respelling is DERIVED from the ipa, not written by hand, so it cannot drift away from what the file actually asks the voice to say.
_readme.unpinned: "ipa": null with "needs_native_speaker": true means nobody here could transcribe it honestly. tools/tts.py drops those terms from the matcher entirely, so the voice reads the spelling as it would anyway. That is deliberate: a confidently wrong <phoneme> sounds authoritative and nobody ever re-checks it, whereas an obviously anglicised reading is something a parent will report. Do not fill these in by guessing - get a speaker.
_readme.matching: tools/tts.py matches case-insensitively, longest term first, on word boundaries, and handles a following possessive 's itself - do not add possessive forms here. Plural forms that actually occur in the stories are listed separately.

Tuaisiala.note: Mizo, Liandova's little brother. The tuai- and -sia- nuclei are in doubt. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

tlawmngaihna.note: Mizo, the ethic of serving first. The tl- onset and aw/ai nuclei need a Mizo speaker. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

khuallam.note: Mizo, the dance of the guests. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

phunchawng.note: Mizo, the silk-cotton tree. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

Tapta.note: Mizo, the frog of the tale. Looks transparent, but Mizo vowel length and tone are not readable from it. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

Sohpetbneng.note: Khasi, the Navel of the Sky hill. The bn- cluster and vowels need a Khasi speaker. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

sohpet.note: Khasi: navel. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

bneng.note: Khasi: sky. The bn- onset cannot be guessed. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

Lum.note: Khasi: hill. Vowel quality (lum/loom) in doubt. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

Diengiei.note: Khasi, the world-shading tree. The -iei nucleus needs a Khasi speaker. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

Klew.note: Khasi, the peacock. The -ew nucleus is not readable from spelling. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

Ksew.note: Khasi, the dog. The ks- onset and -ew nucleus need a speaker. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

Khla.note: Khasi, the tiger. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

iew.note: Khasi: market. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

Hyn.note: Khasi, from Hynniew Trep, the Seven Huts. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

Trep.note: Khasi: hut, from Hynniew Trep. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

Behdienkhlam.note: Pnar, the plague-chasing festival of Jowai. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

beh.note: Pnar: to chase, from Behdienkhlam. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

dien.note: Pnar: stick, from Behdienkhlam. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

khlam.note: Pnar: plague, from Behdienkhlam. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

Aitnar.note: Pnar, the pool where the rots are danced. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

datlawakor.note: Pnar, the wooden-ball game. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

Niamtre.note: Pnar, the Pnar faith. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

Jowai.note: Pnar town. Probably jo-WAI, but not known well enough to pin. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

Pnar.note: The Jaintia people's autonym; the pn- onset cannot be guessed from spelling. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

Jaintia.note: The anglicised district name is said many ways; the community's own reading needs a speaker. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

jingkieng.note: Khasi, the living root bridge (jingkieng jri). NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

jri.note: Khasi: rubber-fig root. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

Nongriat.note: Khasi village of the double-decker bridge. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

Wangala.note: Garo, the hundred-drums festival. Stress and vowels in doubt. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

nokma.note: Garo: the headman. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

Saljong.note: Garo, Misi Saljong the giver. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

Misi.note: Garo, part of Misi Saljong. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

chik.note: Garo, from A'chik, the hill people's autonym; the raised dot is a glottal the engine has no symbol for. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

sungkong.note: Garo, the log drum. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

Twipra.note: Kokborok, the old name of Tripura. The w-vowel cannot be pinned (see Kwrwi). NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

Twi.note: Kokborok: water. Same w-vowel problem as Kwrwi. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

kok.note: Kokborok: speech. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

Borok.note: Kokborok: the people. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

rignai.note: Kokborok, the woven wrap. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

risha.note: Kokborok, the woven stole. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

Chantai.note: Kokborok, the hereditary priests of the Fourteen Gods. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

Subrai.note: Kokborok, Subrai Raja, the eldest god. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

Maliku.note: Mahl, Minicoy's own name. Probably ma-li-ku, but vowel length needs a Mahl speaker. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

Kine.note: Lepcha tale name (Kine Nane). Romanisation cannot be read off reliably - see Mutanchi. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

Nane.note: Lepcha (Kine Nane). NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

Bwisagu.note: Bodo new year. The Bodo w-vowel (Bwisagu ~ Bwisagw) is not representable confidently. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

simolu.note: Assamese silk-cotton tree, often romanised ximolu - the initial sibilant is the Assamese x and cannot be pinned from this spelling. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

barhi.note: Assamese herb from the Goru Bihu chant; the rh cluster is not readable. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

tuhet.note: Nicobarese, the great joint household. Ethnographic romanisation - see Biliku. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

Garo.note: GAA-roh - the people of west Meghalaya
